title: Unify auth header namespace, streaming reconnect policy, and tool-call signing v2
author: Ivy Chen
description:
Motivation: Multiple teams reported inconsistent auth semantics across the HTTP API, streaming endpoints, and the OpenAI-compat layer. This led to flaky reconnects for browser streaming (CORS header gaps), ambiguous precedence when both Authorization and project/org headers are present, and a proliferation of ephemeral token formats for function/tool calls. This PR standardizes the header namespace and parsing order, tightens streaming reconnect semantics to be idempotent, and introduces a second-generation request signing header for tool/function scoped tokens.

What this change does (summary):
- Introduce a consistent header namespace: RW-Project / RW-Org (for explicit project/org headers) and X-RW-Sig (versioned request signature). These are canonical; existing Authorization: Bearer tokens remain supported for backward compatibility and for the OpenAI-compat surface we continue to accept Authorization but with clearer parsing rules (see below).
- Define header precedence: 1) RW-Project / RW-Org (explicit) 2) Authorization: Bearer with explicit prefix (rw_project: or rw_org:) 3) Authorization: Bearer opaque token. This removes ambiguity when multiple auth forms are present.
- Streaming endpoints: add X-RW-Stream-Session (opaque session id) and X-RW-Stream-Sig (session-level signature) and require the server to validate session id + signature on reconnect. CORS preflight updated to expose RW-Project, X-RW-Sig, X-RW-Stream-Session and allow these in Access-Control-Allow-Headers for browser streaming use-cases. This prevents token leakage while enabling reconnects without reauth on bandwidth blips.
- Tool/function calls: introduce scoped claims and signing expectations. Scoped tokens must include scope=tool:NAME or scope=function:NAME. When a scoped token is used to initiate a tool call, clients must send X-RW-Tool-Sig which carries a short-lived HMAC of the call descriptor; servers validate both token scope and tool signature. This enables fine-grained delegation and safe browser usage of tool invocation flows.
- OpenAI compatibility: map OpenAI-Organization to internal RW-Org if present; accept Authorization: Bearer rw_project:<token> as a syntactic sugar mapping to RW-Project header. For private deployments with request-signing enforcement enabled, require X-RW-Sig v2 and reject un-signed opaque Authorization tokens.
- Backwards compatibility: default behavior is backward compatible. New behaviors are gated behind a feature flag (auth.header.v2) and rollout is staged.

Changes included (files): top-level router auth middleware, streaming gateway reconnect handler, CORS policy, token parsing utilities, tests, and documentation updates.

Testing and CI: local unit tests updated for parsing precedence and streaming reconnect. Added integration test that simulates browser streaming reconnects with CORS preflight and signature validation. CI initially failed lint on a naming nit; lint fix was pushed and CI green on the second run. Canary: integration tested in the perf-canary cluster with a limited % of traffic before broad rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag auth.header.v2.
2) Enable for internal staging and run the E2E reconnection harness.
3) Gradually enable on perf-canary for 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours.
4) If metrics stable (no increase in 5xx or reconnection time), enable for all hosted and dedicated. Private customers will be notified 2 weeks before enforcement.

Notes: This PR intentionally separates header semantics from token issuance; token minting and SDK helpers are in follow-up PRs that will consume the new signing libraries. The new X-RW-Sig is compatible with existing HSM/KMS integrations via the signing shim (see commits).
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial refactor of auth middleware; add streaming session signature and CORS changes; tests + docs + lint fixes.
review_comments: Samir: Please confirm that RW-Project header cannot be spoofed in XHRs when credentials are omitted from CORS requests. Also add a note about browser cookie vs header auth differences.

Ivy: Verified - CORS preflight requires Access-Control-Allow-Credentials=true for headers to be sent; we explicitly require that for streaming endpoints. Added docs and tests to demonstrate failure when not present.
Lena: Can we tighten the parsing order so explicit headers always win even if Authorization contains a project prefix? I worry about token confusion during rollouts.
Ivy: Updated parser to prefer explicit RW-Project/RW-Org headers; Authorization with rw_project: is now secondary. Added unit tests to prove precedence.
Tom: The initial CI run failed lint on signer_v2 naming; once fixed, please rebase and squash. Approving once CI is green.
Ivy: Fixed lint and pushed the squash commit. CI green and ready to merge.
release_notes: Standardize auth headers (RW-Project / RW-Org) and introduce X-RW-Sig v2 for request signing; new streaming reconnect headers (X-RW-Stream-Session, X-RW-Stream-Sig); scoped tool/function token signing. Default behavior is backward compatible; enforcement gated by feature flag auth.header.v2. See docs/pkg/api/docs/auth_header_v2.md for migration steps.
backport_instructions: Not required for release branches; this is behind a feature flag. If backporting to release/* for a hotfix, also carry gateway/cors/policy.go and internal/server/auth/middleware.go and ensure feature flag control exists.
notes_for_release_manager: Coordinate with SDK teams: redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-sdk-python follow-ups will publish helpers for RW-Project header and X-RW-Tool-Sig generation. Notify private deploy customers about optional X-RW-Sig enforcement timeline.
qa_steps: 1) Enable auth.header.v2 flag in staging. 2) Run tests/integration/stream_reconnect_test.go. 3) Use browser client to open streaming SSE/WS and simulate network interruption; verify reconnect succeeds without reauth when session header and sig present. 4) Attempt tool invocation with scoped token but mismatched scope; expect 403. 5) Confirm Access-Control-Allow-Headers exposes RW-Project and X-RW-Sig.
authors_notes: Follow-up work: SDK helpers for scoped token creation, documentation for private deploys enforcing X-RW-Sig, and a small telemetry addition to track header usage by clients.
post_merge_tasks: Enable canary rollout in perf-canary for 5% traffic
Open follow-up PR in redwood-sdk-typescript to add helper for X-RW-Tool-Sig
Publish auth_header_v2 docs to the external docs site
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative with immediate enforcement. Operators can toggle enforcement via feature flags; private customers with strict signing requirements will be contacted separately.
